reuse.why: Reuses the matcher's getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance and routes getScheduledAmount through the new helper, but the server sites keep calling getRangedAmount/getWorstCaseAmount behind their own null/number/range dispatch instead of calling getScheduledAmount (or getWorstCaseAmount alone), which already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: The `amount == null ? 0 : typeof amount === 'number' ? getWorstCaseAmount(...) : getRangedAmount(...)` dispatch is edited and kept in updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and normalizeSchedule although getWorstCaseAmount now handles both branches itself.

placement.why: The worst-case rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangedAmount and getScheduledAmount, and the tolerance comes from shared/rules.ts.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the amount computations, tests and a release note; adding an _amountOp field to the forecast's RawScheduleData is necessary plumbing.

maintainability.why: A third positional op argument after a boolean (`getScheduledAmount(amount, false, op)`) is awkward, and the redundant per-site dispatch leaves several places to touch for the next amount-rule change.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule), shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and server/forecast/forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule decide the null/number/range split themselves instead of using getScheduledAmount/getWorstCaseAmount for the whole decision.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated dispatch is the pre-existing ternary left in place with one branch swapped, not reshaped; the approx rule itself is written only once in getWorstCaseAmount.

one_place.where: The approximate-amount rule is defined once in getWorstCaseAmount (shared/schedules.ts), which getScheduledAmount and all the planning/forecast/posting sites call for numeric amounts.
